name: Resourceful
definition: Leaders are frugal and accomplish more with less, recognizing that constraints breed self-sufficiency, invention, and innovation.

rows.situation: When the obvious path is to add spend or headcount
rows.under: Asks for more people or more money before looking at the work.
rows.justRight: Gets the outcome with less, or with a different method, and only then asks for what is still required.
rows.over: Refuses every spend, including the one that would unlock the result.

rows.under: Treats the constraint as a reason the work cannot be done.
rows.justRight: Uses the constraint to invent a simpler path.
rows.over: Romanticizes the constraint and will not remove one that is actually blocking customers.

rows.situation: When a tool or a vendor is the default answer
rows.under: Buys the tool because buying is faster than thinking.
rows.justRight: Asks whether the team can do it with what it has, then buys only what still earns its keep.
rows.over: Rebuilds a commodity in-house to prove self-sufficiency, and the real work waits.

rows.situation: When the budget will not cover the first design
rows.under: Drops the goal to match the budget.
rows.justRight: Redesigns so the goal still holds at the cost you can actually pay.
rows.over: Hides extra spend in another budget so the constraint never has to teach anything.

rows.situation: When the scarce thing is time, not money
rows.under: Spends people's time as if it were free.
rows.justRight: Treats hours like a budget. Cuts low-value work so the important work can finish.
rows.over: Cuts so hard that people have no slack to invent, and the week is only firefighting.
